forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.12. As of May 24, IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits/day through Hormuz — roughly 4% of the ~95-vessel pre-crisis baseline. Lloyd's war-risk premiums remain at 5–8% of hull value (up from ~0.125% pre-war), far above the 1.5% threshold needed to incentivize resumption. Major carriers Maersk (beyond one escorted transit on May 4), MSC, and Hapag-Lloyd have not resumed scheduled commercial service; MSC launched a Hormuz-bypass routing and Hapag-Lloyd has a feeder-avoidance plan in place. The proposed Iran-US MOU (reached May 28, awaiting Trump approval) includes Hormuz reopening terms — mines cleared, no tolls, US blockade lifted — but Trump has requested 'a couple of days' and Iran has not formally confirmed. Vance said on May 29 it is 'TBD.' Even if Trump signs within 48h, mine-clearing operations, insurance market recalibration, and carrier reactivation of Gulf rotations would require additional days. Achieving 50+ vessels/day within any consecutive 7-day window before June 10 is very unlikely absent immediate signature and operational follow-through this weekend.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime (announced May 18) count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.expected_effect: MSC and Hapag-Lloyd have actively launched bypass routes; no scheduled commercial service resumed.

indicators.expected_effect: Formal mechanism for reopening; MOU text agreed at negotiator level but Trump has not signed as of May 30.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No delta allowed — weekly Saturday cadence. Weekly review due Sunday 2026-06-01. Note for Sunday review: (1) DA flagged that the 110-0 preliminary dissolution reading may reflect coordinated coalition management rather than genuine rupture — F2 YES criteria should be reviewed against this scenario; a controlled dissolution bill coordinated by Netanyahu and Haredi parties may not satisfy the 'loss of majority' criterion. (2) Dissolution bill passed preliminary reading 110-0 on May 20; first reading expected June 1. Haredim yielded to Netanyahu's October timeline per Haaretz May 24.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12. A controlled dissolution bill passed by a coalition-coordinated majority does NOT by itself trigger YES — a formal loss of majority or PM resignation is required.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.42. Significant diplomatic movement since May 19. By May 28, US and Iranian negotiators reached agreement on a 60-day MOU text covering: Hormuz reopening, mine clearance, US blockade lift, Iranian oil sales, and a nuclear-negotiations framework. Trump was briefed and told mediators he wants 'a couple of days' to decide. Vance confirmed on May 29 a 'couple of language points' remain. Iran's FM Araghchi called US positions 'a mix of truth and lies' on May 30, maintaining public-facing distance while negotiations remain live. The direct Witkoff–Araghchi meeting indicator has not been confirmed; mediation continued through Qatari channel. Trump has not posted a confirmatory social media statement. The MOU text is agreed at negotiator level — the remaining question is Trump's sign-off and subsequent Iranian principal confirmation within 72h per ambiguity rule. Horizon is June 5 (6 days from update date); window is tight but now materially more plausible than on May 19. Revised to 0.42.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Trump announces approval on June 5 but Iranian confirmation arrives June 6: RESOLVE-NO (horizon is strict EOD June 5).

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO at EOD 2026-05-22. The 45-day Lebanon ceasefire extension was not formally declared void before EOD May 22 by the US State Department or Lebanese FM. The ceasefire was operationally porous — Israeli aircraft conducted thousands of recorded strikes, and IDF chief stated 'there's no ceasefire in south Lebanon' — but the resolution criteria (formal government declaration OR >50 launches/day both sides with US/Lebanon acknowledgment) was not met. Pentagon-hosted Israel-Lebanon military talks opened May 29 with a fourth round scheduled June 2-3, showing the diplomatic channel continued to function through the horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support. IDF chief statement does not constitute US State Dept or Lebanese FM declaration.

indicators.expected_effect: N/A — forecast resolved.

forecasts.question: Will the Israeli Knesset complete a formal final-reading vote to dissolve parliament (not merely a preliminary reading) before EOD 2026-06-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. Dissolution bill passed preliminary reading May 20 (110-0). First reading expected June 1. Netanyahu's preferred timeline is October election; Haredi parties yielded per Haaretz May 24, reducing urgency for fast-track dissolution. Three readings required for final dissolution. Set at 0.55 — coalition controls the schedule and the 110-0 vote confirms cross-coalition procedural support, but Netanyahu has incentive to control pace and maximize Haredi negotiating leverage before final dissolution vote.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset plenum completes a third (final) reading vote on the dissolution bill before EOD June 15, per Times of Israel, Haaretz, or official Knesset records (knesset.gov.il). Resolved NO if no such vote occurs before EOD June 15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Primary: Times of Israel Knesset reporter, Haaretz live Knesset coverage, official Knesset website (knesset.gov.il). Secondary: JNS, i24NEWS.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a vote is held but subsequently challenged legally and not implemented: RESOLVE-YES (the vote itself is the criterion, not implementation). If a vote is scheduled but postponed past June 15 due to coalition breakdown: RESOLVE-NO. A controlled coalition dissolution coordinated by Netanyahu does NOT require a coalition collapse for YES resolution — the vote itself is the only criterion.
